reasons: y/gatewaytls.go puts all Gateway-level TLS in one file: frontendValidation, resolveFrontendValidation, resolveCACertificateRefs, hasInsecureFrontendValidationMode, the new resolveBackendClientCertificate, and the ResolvedRefs condition helpers. x leaves the frontend-validation code in kubernetes.go and adds a separate one-function file, gatewaybackendtls.go, so related Gateway TLS code is split across two files.

x adds gatewaytls.go, which holds all Gateway-level TLS work in one place: frontendValidation, resolveFrontendValidation and resolveCACertificateRefs, the backend client certificate, and the Gateway ResolvedRefs condition. y does structure httproute.go better: the httpRouteBackend type with resolveBackend and loadBackend lets the RequestMirror filter reuse the backend loading cleanly. This is a real point for y, but it does not outweigh x's cleaner split of the Gateway TLS code across files.

y/kubernetes_test.go has a separate Test_makeGatewayStatus_resolvedRefs that matches the extracted function. x adds the client-certificate cases to the existing Test_makeGatewayStatus table, which widens that table's job.

x/httproute.go keeps the retry builder (loadHTTPRouteRetry) next to loadHTTPRouteConfiguration and builds the backendRequest ForwardingTimeouts in one place. y passes a raw time.Duration down through loadWRRService, loadService and loadRequestMirror (which passes 0), and builds the timeout config in loadService.
